subject: MATH
title: Precalculus with Statistics
description: A college-preparatory course that deepens function analysis (polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric), adds vectors, matrices, complex numbers in polar form, sequences, series, and conics, and closes with a substantial statistics strand: data analysis, regression, probability, and inference. Students use Desmos and CODAP throughout and finish with a limits preview and an original statistical investigation.
framework: California Common Core State Standards for Mathematics (Higher Mathematics, including + standards); 2023 California Mathematics Framework (Data Science and Precalculus pathways)

units.title: Functions and Their Transformations
units.big_idea: A small family of parent functions, transformed and combined, models a huge range of situations.

units.title: Polynomial and Rational Functions
units.big_idea: Factors determine zeros, and zeros and asymptotes determine the shape of a graph.

units.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
units.big_idea: Logarithms undo exponentials and let us solve for time in growth and decay.

units.title: Trigonometric Functions
units.big_idea: The unit circle turns angles into coordinates and creates functions that model anything periodic.

units.title: Analytic Trigonometry, Triangles, and Polar Form
units.big_idea: Identities and the Laws of Sines and Cosines extend trigonometry to any triangle and to the complex plane.

units.title: Vectors and Matrices
units.big_idea: Vectors capture magnitude and direction; matrices organize data and solve systems all at once.

units.title: Sequences, Series, and Conic Sections
units.big_idea: Patterns that repeat by addition or multiplication can be summed, and conics are defined by distance.

units.title: Data Analysis and Regression
units.big_idea: Distributions and models summarize variability, but correlation alone never proves cause.

units.title: Probability and Random Variables
units.big_idea: Probability quantifies uncertainty and expected value guides decisions.

units.title: Statistical Inference and Decisions
units.big_idea: Random samples and experiments let us draw conclusions about populations with known uncertainty.

units.title: Limits Preview and Statistics Capstone
units.big_idea: Average rates of change point toward calculus, and a full investigation pulls the year's statistics together.

days.title: Tree diagrams
days.work: Use tree diagrams and the general multiplication rule for drawing cards without replacement.

days.title: Medical testing
days.work: Compute the probability of disease given a positive test (false positives) using a tree and a table; discuss why base rates matter.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a conditional probability quiz.

days.title: Counting principle
days.work: Count license plates, passwords, and outfits with the fundamental counting principle.

days.title: Permutations
days.work: Compute nPr for race finishes and seating arrangements; handle repeated letters.

days.title: Combinations
days.work: Compute nCr for committees and pizza toppings; distinguish when order matters.

days.title: Lottery math
days.work: Compute the probability of winning the California SuperLotto Plus jackpot and compare to everyday risks.

days.title: Quiz
days.work: Take a counting and probability quiz.

objectives: Compute expected value and binomial probabilities

days.title: Distributions
days.work: Define a random variable for the number of heads in 4 flips; build and graph its probability distribution.

days.title: Expected value
days.work: Compute expected values for games of chance and decide whether each game is fair.

days.title: Binomial
days.work: Use the binomial formula and technology to compute probabilities for free-throw and quality-control scenarios.

days.title: Empirical distribution
days.work: Build an empirical distribution from real data (e.g., household size from census tables) and find its mean.

days.title: Unit 9 test
days.work: Take the Unit 9 test on probability.

objectives: Distinguish surveys, experiments, and observational studies

days.title: Populations and samples
days.work: Distinguish parameters from statistics and practice simple random, stratified, and cluster sampling with a random number generator.

days.title: Bias
days.work: Identify voluntary response, undercoverage, nonresponse, and question-wording bias in 8 survey examples.

days.title: Experiments
days.work: Design a randomized experiment (e.g., does music affect memory?) with control, randomization, and replication.

days.title: Evaluate reports
days.work: Critique two news articles that cite statistical studies: what type of study, what conclusions are justified?

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a quiz on study design and bias.

weeks.assessment: Study design quiz and article critiques.

weeks.topic: Simulation, margin of error, and comparing treatments
objectives: Estimate a proportion with margin of error

days.title: Sampling distributions
days.work: Simulate 500 samples in CODAP and observe how sample proportions vary; relate spread to sample size.

days.title: Margin of error
days.work: Compute a 95% margin of error for a poll proportion and interpret the confidence interval.

days.title: Run the experiment
days.work: Carry out your Week 30 memory experiment with at least 10 participants randomly assigned to two groups.

days.title: Randomization test
days.work: Use index cards or CODAP to shuffle group labels 100+ times and decide whether your observed difference is significant.

days.title: Lab report
days.work: Write a lab report with design, results, and a justified conclusion.

objectives: Use expected value to weigh decisions

days.title: Insurance decisions
days.work: Compare expected costs of low vs. high deductible car or health insurance plans.

days.title: Warranties
days.work: Decide whether an extended phone warranty is worth it using expected value and failure probabilities.

days.title: Fair decisions
days.work: Design a fair method to assign chores or choose a winner using random numbers and justify its fairness.

days.title: Product testing
days.work: Analyze a drug-trial or product-testing strategy for false positive/negative tradeoffs.

days.title: Unit 10 test
days.work: Take the Unit 10 test on inference and decisions.

objectives: Connect average rate of change to instantaneous rate

days.title: Approaching a value
days.work: Estimate limits from tables and graphs, including functions with holes.

days.title: Limits algebraically
days.work: Evaluate limits by direct substitution, factoring, and rationalizing for 10 problems.

days.title: Secant to tangent
days.work: Use a Desmos slider to shrink the interval of a secant line and estimate instantaneous rate of change.

days.title: Falling ball
days.work: Video a dropped ball, model height with a quadratic, and estimate its velocity at a moment using shrinking intervals.

days.title: Check
days.work: Take a limits preview quiz.

weeks.topic: Statistics capstone: design and data collection

days.title: Pose a question
days.work: Write a statistical question about your community using a public data set (data.ca.gov) or your own survey/experiment.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Write a data-collection plan naming variables, sampling method, and potential bias.

days.title: Collect
days.work: Collect or download and clean the data (remove duplicates, handle missing values) in CODAP or a spreadsheet.

days.title: Explore
days.work: Create at least three exploratory displays and summary statistics.

days.title: Checkpoint
days.work: Present your question, plan, and initial graphs in a check-in conference.

days.title: Model
days.work: Fit a regression or run a simulation-based comparison appropriate to your question.

days.title: Interpret
days.work: Interpret results in context and list at least three limitations.

days.title: Write report
days.work: Write a 4–6 page statistical report with graphs, methods, and conclusions.

days.title: Build presentation
days.work: Create a 7-minute presentation with your three most important visuals.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the capstone to family or co-op and answer questions.

days.title: Review: functions & trig
days.work: Complete a mixed review of functions, logs, trig, vectors, and matrices.

days.title: Review: statistics
days.work: Complete a mixed review of distributions, regression, probability, and inference.

days.title: Practice final
days.work: Take a timed practice final and correct mistakes.

days.title: Calculus readiness
days.work: Take a calculus-readiness diagnostic and list topics to review this summer.

days.title: Final exam
days.work: Take the cumulative final exam.
